summary: Proceed as a rewrite stage, but only after s6 is harvested with its self-check passing. The 'whatever its score' clause must not cover a failed self-check. Gate BOTH OVL variants at B=1 rather than taking s6's B=16 winner, and print a merge-only DIAG so that a gate miss can be traced to the tile chain or to the 8x-larger two-level merge.
justification: Full verify_1 is 30.3 us (FA3 15.2 + combine 7.2 + prepare 2.8 + norm-gate ~1 + pre-attn 1.5) against a 4.3 us floor, at weight 16 / ~0.24%/us, so about 26 us is replaceable. FINDINGS and the token-group attribution table confirm these numbers. The mechanism is plausible. At B=1, q_len 8 gives 64 query rows per kv head, exactly one m64 wgmma per warpgroup. That removes the mma.sync compute wall that sank full-verify1-sk-two-level-token-group (0.596x gate, row flat 30.0->30.07). For window=0 all 8 tokens share the key range, so the 20 MB are read once. The two-level ticket is proven at decode_1 (27.3->22.6 us; kernel 18.6 us at grid SM). The prior field is honest. s4-batch1 was held on a broken s3 base. The token-group design is mma.sync and is on Do-not-try; the difference here (wgmma, correct s5-derived kernel) is real and is not a retry. DIAGNOSIS action 5 says to do this 'once action 1 routes'. The hypothesis relaxes that to 'whatever its score'. That is acceptable for a rewrite because B=1 is a different regime, but only if s6's kernel passed its self-check. WEAKEST LINK: the latency of each CTA's serial chain, multiplied by too few tiles per CTA. s5 cost about 3.8 us per tile per CTA at B=16 (288.7 us over ~76 tiles/CTA at 2xSM) and about 2.8 us at B=32. At grid SM each CTA owns ~9.5 tiles. Even at a reduced uncontended ~1.5-2 us/tile that is 14-19 us before the merge. And the ring prologue (prefetch distance STAGES_WG-2 = 4, or 10 for OVL=1's 12-stage ring) is about half to all of a CTA's 9.5 tiles, so pipeline fill is never amortised. SECOND: each CTA's partial is 8 tok x 16 heads x 64 fp32 = 32 KB, so ~4.2 MB of partials pass through two merge levels at grid SM (8.4 MB at 2xSM). This is the same 8x-larger merge the token-group reviewer flagged as able to eat the margin, and that design lost. The gate threshold is about 25 us of replaced work at 1.05x. M2 (shape <=22 us) needs a kernel of about 19-20 us, i.e. decode_1's kernel time with 8x the rows and 8x the merge bytes. That is reachable but optimistic. M3 as written (<=15 us) does not match the template milestone (within 1.5x of the 4.3 us floor = ~6.5 us). That floor is unreachable for any design at this tile count; treat M2 as the realistic stage target. The expected flats (verify_16/32 as s6, sliding, decode untouched) match a config-only B==1 route.
confounders: full-verify-wgmma-s6-split-ring-2cta (depends_on, not landed, not yet run): this branch inherits s6's B>1 routing, so verify_16/32 and the headline reflect s6, not s7. Judge s7 only on the full verify_1 row's top_kernels and its PATH CHOSEN line. Judge the B>1 rows against s6's own result, not master or BEST.

full-decode1-streamk-s3-two-level-ticket (landed): it is the source of the two-level ticket. If s7 reuses master's module-level gticket/ticket int32 arrays rather than its own, decode_1 and verify_1 kernels share self-resetting counters. That is safe only while launches are strictly stream-ordered (no PDL overlap between them). Give s7 its own ticket buffers so a future PDL chain cannot corrupt both.

paired-heads-launch-cleanup-ab-tune-batch-gate (landed): it defines the B=1 incumbent as UNPAIRED FA3 + unpaired pre-attention. s7's unpaired-query route matches this, and so does s5's kernel, which takes the unpaired FP8 query. The gate must time exactly master's B=1 path (prepare + FA3 + combine + rms_norm_gate), not the paired path s6 gates against. Otherwise the 1.05x decision is mis-anchored.

fused-preattention-triton (landed): pre-attention stays a separate 1.5 us launch plus a graph-node gap on both sides of the gate, so it cancels. The not-yet-landed V3 chain (fused pre-attn + PDL) showed this gap compounds, so it is headroom left for a later stage, not a confounder.
interference: No companions. This is rewrite stage 7. Its readout is the B=1 printed gate (s7 TWO vs master's unpaired B=1 path), the self-check table and the verify_1 top_kernels, all produced inside one run. The B>1 rows belong to s6 and are judged against s6's result. An ab-revert of any landed hypothesis would not change the B=1 route this stage builds. The one ambiguity a single run can leave is which part of a gate miss (tile chain vs merge) cost the time. A companion run cannot fix that cheaply. An in-run DIAG fixes it: print the kernel time with the merge compiled out (partials written, no ticket/merge) next to the full TWO time, and both OVL variants at grid SM and 2xSM. Also do not select the OVL variant from s6's B=16 winner: B=1 at 9.5 tiles/CTA is latency- and prologue-dominated, so the B=16 ranking does not transfer. Gate both at B=1, use two interleaved rounds at >= 1.05x with an IQR bound (the day's lesson on single-round selectors), and print both.
rules_flags: No rule violation in the plan as written. The route is config-only (B==1, q_len 8, window 0), the gticket arrays are self-resetting int32 buffers (allowed), the merges are fp32, the output is bf16, and every key is attended.

Two-level ticket correctness depends on the last arriver merging, never on spinning for co-resident CTAs. OVL=1 at 2xSM (1 CTA/SM) would not be co-resident, so confirm no CTA waits on another's progress.

If s6 never built and s7 builds s6's OVL=0 variant itself, the same build must carry s6's full bisect and two-state replay before any B=1 route. The import clock is already 222 s over 4 modules: give the module its own deadline and fall back to master on overrun.

If gticket is indexed gticket[c_b*32 + gi] with Gs = ceil(sqrt(nseg)), grid 2xSM (264) gives 17 groups (< 32). Assert the group count <= 32 at the shape/config level for any grid used, including the 3/7 self-check grids.
open_questions: Has s6 run and passed its self-check? If s6 failed its self-check, s7 must wait for an s6 fix rather than build on it. That is the exact failure that held s4-batch1.

What is s5/s6's per-tile chain latency on an idle SM (B=1, grid SM)? A one-line DIAG at B=1 with GATHER_ONLY vs full compute would show whether the 9.5-tile chain alone exceeds the ~25 us gate threshold before the merge is added.
Should the last-group merge spread the 8 tokens x 16 heads over all 256 threads, or over multiple finalizer CTAs (one per token), to keep the 4.2 MB merge off a single CTA's critical path?

Is grid SM really optimal at B=1 for a 64-row wgmma tile? With prologue depth ~4-10 tiles, a 2xSM or 3xSM grid with a shallower ring may beat SM. Consider adding grid 2xSM for OVL=1 with STAGES_WG reduced as well.
